messages:
bob_cust: Hey team — we filed a DELETE for customer dataset `proj-9812` yesterday via the API but it's still showing in the console and audit logs. Delete API returned 202. Need an accelerated purge; can you confirm timeline? :worried:

alice_support: Sorry for the trouble — can you paste the request ID or the exact timestamp you called the delete? 202 response means queued, but should include a `request_id` in response headers.

bob_cust: request-id: r-72a9f3c4, called at 2026-06-04T18:03:10Z. We need it removed ASAP — regulatory deadline.

alice_support: Got it, thanks. I'm escalating to SRE and Security. Setting expectation: default retention for user data is 30 days after deletion, but there are exceptions (legal holds, export jobs, and KMS/HSM key windows). I'll update once I hear back. :eyes:

david_sre: Looking in the deletion queue now. I can see r-72a9f3c4 accepted by the delete-processor at 18:03:11Z. However the physical purge step is waiting on key-unwrap confirmation from our HSM cluster (key id: kms-05f). There's a pending rotation job that blocks zeroization for that key.

carmen_security: To clarify: keys in the HSM have a small window where we retain wrapped key material until rotation completes to ensure previous decrypts for in-flight ops succeed. That window is usually <=48 hours, but in rotation edge-cases we can see longer delays. Is the dataset under a legal hold? @eva_legal can confirm.

eva_legal: No active legal hold on proj-9812 in our records. Customer submitted a separate eDiscovery request last month but it was closed. No holds currently.

bob_cust: Ok — so if there's no legal hold, can we force a key zeroization now? This is time-sensitive. What are the risks?

david_sre: Forcing zeroization will invalidate any ciphertext encrypted under that key. If any background export/archival job still referencing those ciphertexts exists, they'll fail. We can schedule an immediate zeroize with an ops runbook, but we need sign-off from Security and Legal because it is irreversible.

carmen_security: We can approve immediate zeroization for this key if Legal signs off. Also need customer confirmation that they accept the irreversible nature. Please confirm in-thread. :lock:

bob_cust: We confirm. We accept irreversible deletion now. Please proceed.

eva_legal: I'll record authorization. Quick note: capture audit evidence before zeroize. Retention_bot: generating evidence package...

retention_bot: [automated] evidence_package_id=ep-20260604-18-22 created; includes API request/response, queue logs, and current audit entries. URL: https://redwood.example/evidence/ep-20260604-18-22 (internal only)

david_sre: Starting zeroization run now. Runbook snippet: ```
# zeroize key kms-05f
notify: all-teams
backup: create-temporary-audit-export --id ep-20260604-18-22
hsm_cmd: hsm zeroize --key kms-05f --confirm
```

alice_support: I'll keep the customer updated. Running pre-checks on exports and replay queues to make sure nothing will reference the key after zeroize.

david_sre: Zeroize completed at 18:42:17Z. Post-zeroize check: all services that tried to access the key returned KMS:KeyNotFound. No failing jobs in the last 10m observed.

alice_support: I can confirm dataset `proj-9812` is no longer visible in the console and audit index shows a deletion event + zeroize marker.

bob_cust: Thank you — can you share the full deletion/audit IDs for our compliance evidence?

alice_support: Sure — deletion request r-72a9f3c4, evidence package ep-20260604-18-22, zeroize event z-1822505670. I'll email the export bundle to the security contact you provided.

bob_cust: Received. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

carmen_security: Note for internal follow-up: we'll add a post-mortem on the key rotation edge-case and reduce the rotation hold window. Filing ticket INF-4123.

david_sre: Ticket created and linked to the runbook. Closing thread once export delivered. :white_check_mark:
